messages.subject: Re: Web Development with R
messages.body_plain:
If Node.js works on Windows, you might be OK with Shiny Server.
However, you should also consider using the native Windows hypervisor,
Hyper-V, hosting a Linux web server with whatever software you can
deploy in an effective manner.

By the way, Apache itself - indeed, the whole "LAMP" stack, can run on
Windows. So I'm not sure why you couldn't run rApache on a Windows
server.

On Tue, Mar 5, 2013 at 11:30 AM, Jeroen Ooms <jeroe...@gmail.com> wrote:
> Windows is not suitable for building web stacks. We are trying to help you
> when we advise you to at least install vmware player with a small linux
> server. Really, its not that hard.

I did a bit of benchmarking of Linux servers running on Windows 8 Pro
with the installed Client Hyper-V virtualizer, VirtualBox and VMware
Workstation. VirtualBox was slow enough to be out of the running, but
both Hyper-V and VMware Workstation had "acceptable" performance on a
CPU-bound (Redis) workload. I can't publish numbers - VMware's license
strictly-interpreted prohibits it, and I am not willing to take them
or Microsoft on in court.

But I disagree with a blanket assertion that Windows is not suitable
for building web stacks. There are lots of options, including "native"
- Windows Server, IIS, .NET, ASP, etc., and BitNami stacks to name
just two. The decision to use a Linux server running under a
hypervisor rather than native or BitNami is going to depend on overall
business goals and cost tradeoffs, of course.

You'll need to do your own benchmarking, too. And once you go down the
hypervisor path, you need to consider the native Hyper-V as well as
VMware, and I don't think VMware Player is really a good way to deploy
Linux servers, even small ones, on a Windows machine. You can't take
snapshots with VMware Player, for example.

--

I was suggesting vmware player only as a local development solution to get started if for whatever reason you are stuck with windows. In production you should be using some virtualization (kvm, xen) or private cloud solution (openstack), or spin up a cloud instance (which you'll find surprisingly easy to do with linux).

Other than that I can only wish you good luck in dealing with licenses and companies that apparently threaten to sue you. It sounds like a pretty dysfunctional relationship to me :-)

messages.subject: Plots in RApache(Client-server model)
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I am using RApache on a Ubuntu system, and accessing it through my browser on the Windows system. The normal R codes are working fine, problem comes when I am trying Plotting.

This is the code am using in the file /var/www/R/code(the folder has full permissions and ownership)

setContentType("image/png")
t <- tempfile()
x <- c(1,3,6,9,12)
y <- c(1.5,2,7,8,15)
png(t,type="cairo")
plot(x,y)
dev.off()
sendBin(readBin(t,'raw',n=file.info <http://file.info>(t)$size))
unlink(t)

This is my httpd.conf file,

<Location /rapachetest>
        SetHandler r-handler
        RFileHandler /var/www/R/code
</Location>

When i open the brower, http://Ip_addr_of_server/rapachetest, I get some page which displays "internal server error'.

The apache log file shows this,

Error in X11(paste("png::", filename, sep = ""), g$width, g$height, pointsize,  : unable to start device PNG
In addition: Warning messages:
1: In readLines(file) : incomplete final line found on '/var/www/R/code'
2: In png(t, type = "cairo") : unable to open connection to X11 display ''

Traceback:
1: png(t, type = "cairo")
[Fri Mar 08 14:25:39 2013] [error] [client 107.108.207.104] File does not exist: /var/www/favicon.ico

I have built R with x11 and PNG support.
Please help regarding this
Thanks in advance
--
Regards

Vijeth Hegde

messages.subject: Re: Problems configuring rApache on Ubuntu 12.04 -- Which .conf files do I need to edit?
messages.subject_clean: Problems configuring rApache on Ubuntu 12.04 -- Which .conf files do I need to edit?
messages.body_plain:
The standard way of configuring Apache in Ubuntu is using config
includes. Usually you create a file

/etc/apache2/mods-available/mod_R

that contains:

LoadModule R_module /usr/lib/apache2/modules/mod_R.so

You can then enable or disable this module using

sudo a2enmod mod_R
sudo a2dismod mod_R

These command will create symlinks in /etc/apache2/mods-enabled/ which
are actually sourced by the main httpd.conf

In a similar way, you can create a site, e.g to create a site 'rinfo':

/etc/apache2-sites-available/rinfo

that contains:

 <Location /RApacheInfo>
      SetHandler r-info
 </Location>

You can then enable/disable this site using:

sudo a2ensite rinfo
sudo a2dissite rinfo

After reloading rapache you should be able to visit http://localhost/RApacheInfo

messages.subject: rapache 1.2.3 ubuntu builds
messages.body_plain:
I published some new builds for rapache on ubuntu (for precise,
quantal and raring). To install:

sudo add-apt-repository ppa:opencpu/rapache
sudo apt-get update
sudo apt-get install libapache2-mod-r-base

This will automatically install and enable mod_R. To uninstall:

sudo apt-get purge libapache2-mod-r-base

The repository currently contains:
  - R 2.15.3.
  - rApache 1.2.3

To remove this repository from your system, you can do:

sudo rm sudo rm /etc/apt/sources.list.d/opencpu-rapache*
sudo apt-get update
